steps.text: Rinse the pieces of {cod}, lay them skin side up in a deep dish and cover them with cold {water}. Keep the dish in the fridge and change the {water} several times, until a flake from the thickest part tastes lightly seasoned.
Drain the {cod} and pat it dry on every side with a clean cloth.

Warm the {olive-oil} in the pan on the lowest heat with the {garlic} [guindilla: and the {guindilla}], until the {garlic} is pale gold and smells sweet and has not browned. Lift out the {garlic} [guindilla: and the {guindilla}] and keep them.

Slip the {cod} into the scented {olive-oil}, skin side down, with the heat very low. The {olive-oil} must barely stir. Leave the pieces in it until the flesh turns opaque and a milky liquid starts to seep from the flakes, then lift the {cod} out onto a plate. Do not salt anything.

Let the {olive-oil} cool until it is just warm and pour it into a jug, leaving the milky juices in the pan. Put the {cod} back skin side up. Shake the pan slowly in small circles on and off a very low heat, and pour the {olive-oil} back in a thin thread, a little at a time, as the juices turn pale and thick. Stop when the sauce is creamy and clings to the fish. Here the {olive-oil} goes back in a little at a time, where the usual card starts with a little {olive-oil} in the pan.
Spoon the sauce over the {cod} and scatter the golden {garlic} [guindilla: and the {guindilla}] on top.
